answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 72% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned so that nobody profits from it. Because the velvet forfeiture is applied at exit, the terrace ledger totals each burn, and the juniper audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 187 aliases therefore destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 8 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
